sweep_method: For each block I swept for siblings by grepping the contract for every other statement that reuses the same premise (device-in-descriptor, byte-parity, the provisional note, crate enumerations) and confirmed each sibling against the tree: `grep -rn 'issues/500'` over ci/ .github/ deploy/ docs/ crates/; `grep -rn 'jammi-lora'` over *.py/*.sh/*.yml/*.md/*.txt to enumerate every file that lists crates by name; the governance-stem matcher replayed over all 19 declared pub names.

grep over the diff's prose surfaces for each claim's key phrase ('ListWorkers', 'matching device', 'max_world_size', 'local_ranks', 'no placement', 'fixed port', 'feat_500-wave4', 'context_predictor'), then manual read of every implementing site (worker.rs placement/topology/holder paths, config/mod.rs BallistaConfig + DistributedConfig validators, placement.rs/client.rs/engine.rs/roles.rs/codec.rs, jobs_repo.rs transfer_claim + upsert_worker + list_workers, schema.rs migration 038, job.proto/grpc/job.rs) and cross-read of every shape-d manifest and both ConfigMaps against each other

git diff --stat + full read of every prose-bearing hunk; targeted greps across docs/, deploy/, CHANGELOG.md and crates/*/src for each mechanism token the fixes touched ('Awaiting', 'max_world_size'/'serveable_world', 'device_kind'/'K7', 'GangExec { job_id', 'ordinal order', 'addresses_collide', 'admit_training_spec'); a python scan of every .rs file in the diff for tautological assert_eq!/assert!(true); an empirical two-line cargo clippy run in doclens2-scratch to pin clippy::eq_op's default level

(a) Awaiting-order class: grep over crates/, docs/, deploy/, CHANGELOG.md for 'after a successful submit', 'after submitting', 'right after submit', 'once submitted', 'has SUBMITTED', 'after the submit', plus a full grep of 'Awaiting' in all tracked .md — each hit opened and compared to crates/jammi-ai/src/fine_tune/worker.rs:2219-2234. (b) Citation class: python regex over docs/maintainer/*.md for basename-form `file.ext:N` not preceded by a path (11 hits, exhaustive for that root), each resolved against the pinned da406662 export; established the resolver's blind spot by reading ci/scripts/perf/check_citations.py:574-584 and :1823-1863 and by running the checker itself (green). (c) Stale-enumeration class: read both workflow files end to end and re-checked every count/enumeration the diff touches (api-stability.md:150, CHANGELOG entries, README/overlay replica and GPU counts). Tree pinned via `git archive da406662` into /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-vijaychakilam-git-f-inverse-jammi-ai/633b7b0f-9596-44a5-a195-cb45cfc23fc9/scratchpad/doclens3-scratch/t_da406662 after the lead's worktree advanced to 6e717f1c mid-audit.

grep over the pinned tree at 306c9d55 for each class: (i) 'stops task admission|task admission at once|stop admitting new|refuse what.s new' over docs/ deploy/ crates/, plus 'grep -rn "\.drain()" crates/jammi-server/src crates/jammi-ballista/src' for the code root; (ii) 'upsert_compute_executor(|register_executor(|remove_compute_executor(|remove_executor(' over every crates/**/tests file, mapped registration->removal per test fn, then the backing read traced to compute_repo.rs's SELECT; (iii) 'NATIVE_COMPUTE_CAP' and 'RP_CLUSTER_GPU_TYPE|RP_CLUSTER_MIN_AVAILABILITY' over ci/ and .github/, plus A100 mentions in the cluster lane's own docs. Both executable gates re-run: check_gpu_prove_once.py OK, test_gpu_cluster_lane.sh 88/0.

grep -rn 'TERMINATING' over crates/ plus the vendored ballista-executor/ballista-scheduler 54.1.0 sources (the static, its single writer, its reader at executor_server.rs:317, the scheduler's get_alive_executors); grep -rn '\.begin_drain()|\.drain()' over crates/*/tests to enumerate every test that can reach the flip, then a read of each hit to separate session-scoped HostAdmission::begin_drain and serve-control drain() from ExecutorRole's; a read of crates/jammi-ballista/tests/it/main.rs and Cargo.toml's [[test]] targets to establish which binaries share a process. runtime.rs:1260/1398/1464 are the production call sites through which crates/jammi-server/tests/it/ballista_roles.rs:81 flips the same static in the jammi-server `it` binary — pre-existing (the pre-round `drain()` flipped it in the same test), and it is the only executor-hosting test in that binary today, so it has no victim yet; it is listed because any future executor-hosting test added there inherits the defect. roles_drain.rs:69 is the correctly isolated reference member.

Per-hunk read of the full 808-line code diff plus the docs diff; identifier greps across crates/ and docs/ for `cluster_state`, `registered_executor_metadata`, `EXECUTOR_LIVENESS_WINDOW`, `executor_is_live`, `placement_available`, `with_owned_rows`, `owned.borrow_mut().push`, `begin_drain`, `Crashable`; counted with_owned_rows call sites (12 = 1 def + 11 uses) against the 11 registering tests; re-read every re-anchored citation line in the pinned tree; two executed probes — (1) a bash probe driving the lane's own run_wait_two_reads mock against a reverted copy of runpod_gpu_cluster.sh, (2) a minimal rustc compile confirming the dead_code lint on a written-never-read struct field. No cargo.

grepped 'tenant' across crates/jammi-ballista and the whole 0e11162a..HEAD diff; read the universe/allowlist of both enumerating tenant oracles (tenant_isolation_oracle.rs, gang_rank_admission_oracle.rs); enumerated every new listener from roles.rs and checked each for an interceptor/TLS layer; grepped 'ballista' across docs/guide/src/security.md and deploy-server.md to falsify the I-PEER trust-class justification; read the three TenantBinding::admin_scope sites in the new crate and cleared them (compute_jobs has no tenant column; the placement read consumes only jobs.claimed_by in the deny direction)

Beyond the mechanical gates I swept three closed classes by hand. (1) Every decode arm in crates/jammi-ballista/src/codec.rs:155-159 (Inference, AnnSearch, AsofJoin, KeyCheck, Gang) for a tenant-parameterized catalog read: only AnnSearch performs one, and it is the covered site. (2) Every catalog call site in crates/jammi-ballista/src (grep '.catalog()' -> client.rs:51 list_compute_executors, roles.rs:584/590 get/upsert_compute_executor, codec.rs:352): the first three read compute_executors, which migration 038 creates with no tenant_id — cluster-plane rows of the same class as instances/workers, not tenant-isolated reads. The placed-gang job read (crates/jammi-ai/src/fine_tune/worker.rs:2440) is deliberately admin-scoped and documented as such, matching the pre-existing claim loop and the already-allowlisted I-GANG peer surface, not a new escalation class. (3) Every service mounted by crates/jammi-ballista/src/roles.rs (:127/144 SchedulerGrpc, :509/512 FlightService, :561 ExecutorGrpc) against the three BALLISTA_LISTENER_ALLOWLIST entries — three for three, and no add_service/Routes addition anywhere in crates/jammi-server/src. No sibling site carries the blocked violation.
